profile.headline: Software & Data Engineer | Python, C++, FastAPI | Data Pipelines, APIs, ML/Computer Vision
profile.summary:
Software and data engineer with experience building and modernizing production systems in C++ and Python, from backend APIs and legacy-system integration to large-scale data pipelines, Linux infrastructure, CI/CD, and cloud deployments.

I currently develop software for University of Idaho IT, where I am architecting the backend modernization of a legacy C++ CGI application into a FastAPI-based architecture. I also rebuilt and maintain the campus network-data ingestion service, which polls Cisco, Juniper, and SNMP sources every six minutes across ~3,500 access points, ~350 switches, and >150K unique client MACs and feeds campus DHCP/DNS configuration.

My previous research work at Washington State University spanned scientific software and data engineering: multi-terabyte imaging and spectroscopy pipelines, reproducible data lineage, Python/OpenCV measurement tools, PyTorch computer-vision workflows, and statistical analysis and visualization in Python and R.

More recently, I have been applying that engineering background to LLM systems, building a job-search platform with local and hosted inference, structured outputs, gold-labeled evaluation datasets, versioned prompts, CI, and per-run cost tracking.

I work comfortably across software, data, and infrastructure boundaries and am interested in software engineering, backend, data engineering, research software, and ML-adjacent roles where that breadth is useful.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Contracted through Magnus Wood Solutions LLC to modernize and maintain production software and data systems for University of Idaho IT Net Team.

Architecting the backend modernization of a legacy C++ CGI application, defining the FastAPI REST contract and canonical Pydantic schema while building the FastAPI/C++ boundary that isolates a React frontend from a 30-year-old BerkeleyDB datastore.

Rebuilt and now maintain the campus network-data ingestion platform, adding validation, structured logging, error handling, automated testing, and modular vendor integrations across Cisco, Juniper Mist, and SNMP sources. The service polls every 6 minutes across ~3,500 access points, ~350 switches, and >150K unique client MACs and drives campus DHCP/DNS configuration.

Designed a vendor-abstraction layer enabling Cisco IOS-XE and Juniper Mist APIs to coexist with legacy SNMP collection, reducing integration time for new hardware from weeks to days.

Modernized engineering practices across the long-running C++ codebase with Git workflows, CI, automated testing, developer documentation, and Docker-based deployments.

positions.title: Scientific Assistant
positions.description:
Over 14 years in the Kirchhoff Lab and IBC Phenomics Center, my role evolved from scientific instrumentation and experimental support into data engineering, research software, computer vision, and machine learning.

Data engineering — Designed and operated multi-TB imaging and spectroscopy pipelines covering ingestion, validation, transformation, partitioned storage, metadata, and downstream analysis.

Research software & computer vision — Built Python/OpenCV tools for interactive image annotation and quantitative fluorescence analysis, turning researcher-defined regions and metadata into reproducible measurements for downstream statistics.

Reproducibility — Built data-lineage and metadata systems that let published results be traced back to their original measurements years later, supporting peer review and outlier investigation.

ML & analysis — Trained PyTorch segmentation/classification models, scaled larger training jobs to Azure, and integrated inference into standard analysis workflows. Analyzed and visualized phenomics data in Python and R and presented findings to researchers and project stakeholders.

Mentoring — Mentored students and research staff in software tools, instrumentation, experimental workflows, testing, documentation, and reproducible data practices.
positions.insights: Data Engineering, Python (Programming Language) and +10 skills

projects.title: AI-Powered Job Search & Tracking System — Azure & Linux
projects.description: Automation harness for applied LLM agents: scrapes and dedupes job postings, then runs a pipeline of LLM classifiers to filter and rank roles against a candidate profile. Uses local inference (llama.cpp/ollama) or the OpenAI API with structured Pydantic outputs, running the same pipeline locally and in Azure (hybrid ops), fronted by a React/TypeScript app with Entra ID (OIDC) auth. Built an evaluation framework with gold-labeled sets, versioned prompts, and per-run cost tracking.

projects.title: Cloud Compute & Storage Operations — Azure & AWS
projects.description: Hands-on operation of cloud compute and storage across Azure and AWS: ran PyTorch model training jobs on Azure with associated blob storage; provisioned and operated AWS-hosted services end-to-end (VM lifecycle, networking, backups). Working knowledge of cloud cost, deployment, and operational tradeoffs from real use.
